steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Land = all natural resources (farmland, oil, water). Reward: rent. Labour = human effort and skills. Reward: wages. | Key Fact: Capital = man-made resources used in production (machinery, factories). Reward: interest. Enterprise = the entrepreneur who organises and takes risk. Reward: profit. | Key Fact: Scarcity means resources are limited but wants are unlimited — the fundamental economic problem that forces choices. | Key Fact: Opportunity cost is the benefit of the next best alternative foregone when making a choice. E.g. if government spends on defence, the opportunity cost is the healthcare that could have been funded instead.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Identify the four factors of production and the reward each receives. | Explain what is meant by scarcity and why it is the fundamental economic problem. | A government has £10bn to spend on hospitals OR schools. Explain the opportunity cost of choosing hospitals.
